transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Carla Colman.
Congress only has a few weeks to pass spending legislation or the federal government will
partially shut down.
A group of Senate Democrats wants to block funding for the Iran war.
They're thinking about putting a provision in the must-pass spending bill that would
block Iran war spending, but Republicans oppose this.
There are concerns that could create a stalemate and that could lead to a shutdown.
Wisconsin Republican Senator Ron Johnson says he's concerned that could happen.
I hope not.
I hope not.
I mean, I'm sure every Republican senator will vote for another continuing resolution
if you can't do it through appropriation.
Do we have seven Democrats that are willing to join us and not shut down the government
and not do such damage?
This is continuing resolutions are particularly damaging to the defense of this nation.
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
President Trump says he'll hold a press conference in a few hours at the White House.
He says he'll talk about his just completed trip to Asia.
The Trump administration is urging a federal judge to let it close the Kennedy Center for
two years.
NPR's Anastasia Tsiolkas has more.
editors representing the Trump administration urged Judge Christopher Cooper to let the arts
institution close its main complex for a $257 million renovation.
They argued that the renovation plans have been sufficiently scrutinized by the center's
board, which is chaired by President Trump and is mostly made up of his allies.
In September, Trump renewed his threat to tear the center down if his name is not added
to it.
The next marquee event is next month, the annual Kennedy Center honors, which are now
slated to be held at Washington's Capital One Arena.
CBS will air the ceremony on December 27.
It will also stream on Paramount Plus, Anastasia Tsiolkas, NPR News.
Houthi rebels in Yemen say they have targeted Saudi Arabia's financial district with cruise
missiles.
Saudi Arabia's Emergency Response Agency has confirmed an attack on an 80-story tower
that it says also damaged nearby buildings, and PR's Ayah Batrawi has more.
The Houthis who are backed by Iran say they fired missiles that struck the Saudi capital
Riyadh's financial district and other parts of Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia's military spokesman confirmed missile threats on Riyadh and said debris had
caused material damage from one of those attacks.
Then Saudi Arabia's Emergency Response Agency posted a photo showing windows blown out and
damage across several floors of the Public Investment Fund Tower, named after the Kingdom
Sovereign Wealth Fund.
People in the financial district have been working remotely, and there were no reports
of casualties.
The Houthis say their attacks are in response to deadly Saudi airstrikes, including one
on a hotel in Yemen's Red Sea city of Mocha that killed 10 people Thursday.
Ayah Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
You're listening to NPR News.
Heavy rain has pummeled Florida's Atlantic coast this week and flood cautions are still
up.
The National Weather Service says the area, around Fort Lauderdale, got nearly 17 inches
of rain in nearly two days.
There are more flood concerns and warnings in California.
Heavy rain has been falling in the San Francisco Bay area.
The video game Grand Theft Auto VI has already made around $2 billion, NPR's James Mastrom
Marino reports it was released yesterday.
Grand Theft Auto VI is the first game in the controversial crime video game series in 13
years.
Finally, so excited.
GTA VI takes place in a fictionalized version of Miami called Vice City.
Real life buildings and streets appear in the game, while Miami itself has rebranded
as Vice City in a multi-million dollar marketing campaign.
It's just a sliver of its estimated budget of around $1 billion.
The investment is paying off.
The game's on track to earn more than $3 billion within its first week.
And this is only the beginning.
Experts project that Grand Theft Auto VI will make billions of dollars for years to come.
James Mastrom Marino, NPR News.
The Cincinnati Zoo says its beloved hippo, Fiona, has died.
She had eaten a visitor's hat.
Zoo keepers had waited for nature to take its course, but there were complications.
After several attempts, zoo veterinarians say they were not able to help her.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.
